title: Wang 2-corner tiles + dual grid — engine module + Kaboom Crew floor migration (replaces 4-edge approach for floors)
intent: Per `docs/game-design/wang-2corner-design.md`. The 4-edge Wang shipped S169/S170/S176 produces grid-aligned tile boundaries — adjacent terrain types meet with crisp seams ('набор кубов' feel). User asked for 'прекрасную систему тайлинга чтоб уровни смотрелись живо и красиво'. The proper answer (per Joe Strout + Boris The Brave articles): 2-corner Wang with DUAL GRID. Render tiles sit at CORNERS between 4 logical cells (offset by +0.5 from logical grid). Each render tile's 4-corner bitmask determines mesh + rotation. Inter-family blends become FREE — grass curves into path through tile geometry, not by snapping to next cell. Result: arena reads as ORGANIC TERRAIN, not GRID-ALIGNED PATCHES. Cliff faces + block walls stay on 4-edge approach (less benefit); ONLY floor tiles migrate.
rationale: Source: user-provided articles (Joe Strout dev.to + Boris The Brave) + `docs/game-design/wang-2corner-design.md` (this batch). Architecturally SUPERSEDES the 4-edge approach for floor cells. Per `feedback-game-design-authority` memory — design wins over shipped code; dev rewrites floor rendering. Cliff/block code stays unchanged. Cost: medium-large — new engine module + project re-registration + ~5 new mesh shapes per family. ~400 LOC engine + 300 LOC kaboom-side + new family mesh authoring.
acceptanceHints: READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/wang-2corner-design.md` — canonical spec for the 2-corner approach + dual grid offset + family priority order + tile variant tables.
ENGINE MODULE — NEW `engine/render/autotile-2corner/`:
Sits ALONGSIDE existing `engine/render/autotile/` (4-edge module from S169). Both stay available.
Schema files (under `schemas/components/`):
render-tile-2corner.schema.json — RenderTile2Corner component { rgx, rgz, family, cornerBitmask, currentVariantIndex, currentRotationYDeg, currentMeshKey }
wang-corner-tile-family.schema.json — WangCornerTileFamily { name, variants[16], priority, defaults? }
Family registry (engine/render/autotile-2corner/family-registry.ts):
registerWangCornerFamily(family) + lookups + priority order via registerFamilyPriorityOrder([...]).
Resolver (engine/render/autotile-2corner/render-tile-resolver-system.ts):
For each render-grid position (rgx, rgz): look up the 4 logical cells at corners NW, NE, SE, SW.
Determine primary family for this render tile via priority-order tie-break.
Compute corner bitmask (4 bits, each set if that corner's cell == primary family).
Look up variant + rotation in primary family's 16-variant table.
Write RenderTile2Corner component.
Per logical-cell family change: re-resolve the 4 surrounding render tiles.
Render-grid dimensions = logical-grid + 1 in each axis (corners extend one beyond cells at arena perimeter).
KABOOM CREW SIDE — FLOOR MIGRATION:
examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/register-wang-families.ts: register the 5 floor families (grass / path / stone / dirt / floor) using the 2-CORNER pattern.
Hard blocks + soft blocks + cliff faces STAY on the 4-edge approach (per §6.2 hybrid support — these benefit less from corner-blending).
Family priority order registered: ['floor', 'dirt', 'path', 'grass', 'stone'] — stone wins ties, floor loses. So a grass-meets-stone corner renders stone with grass curving into stone.
MESH BUILDERS — extend per-family builders (extends GDP-2026-05-29-007 grass + GDP-2026-05-29-005 per-biome batch):
16 builders per family (instead of 4-5 from before). Builders index by corner bitmask 0..15.
Many bitmasks share base geometry with rotation. E.g. bitmask 1 (NW corner only) and bitmask 2 (NE corner only) use the same INNER-CORNER mesh rotated 90°.
Implementation: ~5 base shapes per family × 4 rotations + 1 filler (bitmask 15) + 1 empty (bitmask 0 falls through to next-priority family).
Base shapes per family:
INNER-CORNER (variants 1, 2, 4, 8) — small corner curve, one corner is this family, surrounded by non-family.
HALF (variants 3, 6, 9, 12) — half-and-half split, this family on one half.
DIAGONAL (variants 5, 10) — opposite corners are this family. Saddle / checker.
OUTER-CORNER (variants 7, 11, 13, 14) — three corners this family, one corner non-family.
FILLER (variant 15) — all 4 corners this family.

Each family customises these 5 shapes with biome-specific detail (grass blades curve at the corners, stone bevels sharply, etc.) — per GDP-2026-05-29-007 grass rewrite + GDP-2026-05-29-005 biome geometry approach.
RENDERER COMPOSITION:
Render tile entity per render-grid position. Mesh entity child-parented; uses Transform.position = (logical_x + 0.5, logical_y, logical_z + 0.5) — sitting at corner between 4 logical cells.
Each render tile mesh is 1×0.20×1 — same dimensions as current floor cells, just offset.
Logical cells (FloorTerrain components) UNCHANGED — they store data only. Visual lives in RenderTile2Corner mesh entities.
INTER-FAMILY BLENDS (the main feature):
A render tile at corner of [grass, grass, path, path] resolves as:
Primary family by majority + priority: grass + path tie, priority says path > grass, so primary = path.
Corner bitmask vs path: [non-path, non-path, path, path] = 0011 binary = bitmask 3 = SOUTH half tile from path family.
Path family's south-half variant renders: visually a path-tile with smooth grass-curving on the north half.
The CURVE between grass and path is baked into the path mesh's north-half shape — geometry handles the transition organically.
DOCTOR INTEGRATION:
Engine doctor reports both Wang modules: '4-edge: M families, K cells' AND '2-corner: N families, R render tiles'.
MULTIPLAYER (server-authoritative gameplay from S125):
Server's logical grid + family-membership is unchanged. Server doesn't need to know about render tiles (they're client-side visual).
Each client runs its own 2-corner resolver. Visually consistent across tabs (deterministic).
DETERMINISM: corner-bitmask computation + priority resolution deterministic per (logical grid state + family priority order). Bot-vs-bot regression test continues to resolve.
PERFORMANCE BUDGET:
Render-grid is (W+1) × (H+1) tiles = ~10% more than logical grid. At 17×17 cross arena: 324 render tiles vs 289 logical cells. Negligible.
Mesh resolution at scene-load: O(render-tile-count) = ~1ms total.
Per-event re-resolve: 4 render tiles per logical change. Cheap.
TESTS:
Logical grid 2×2 all grass → render grid 3×3, primary family = grass on inner tile, edge tiles resolve to grass-with-inner-curve.
Logical grid mixed grass + path on a checker pattern → render tiles resolve to diagonal-blend variants.
Family priority tie-break: 2 grass + 2 path corners → priority says path > grass, primary = path.
Re-resolve on logical change: change one logical cell's family → 4 render tiles re-resolve to new bitmasks.
Backwards compat: cells without FloorTerrain default to 'floor' family — old arenas render correctly.
VISUAL QA:
Load grassland arena with grass + path mix → boundaries SMOOTHLY CURVE through tile interiors, no grid-aligned seams.
Bombers walking across a grass-path boundary visually cross a soft transition, not a hard line.
Compare side-by-side with 4-edge version → 2-corner clearly organic / 4-edge clearly grid-aligned.
DOCS UPDATES (in this PR):
wang-tile-autotile-design.md — mark as 'legacy for cliff + block walls'. 2-corner is the floor path.
wang-2corner-design.md — mark as 'shipped' once this lands. Note any deviations from spec.
visual-style.md §9 — update arena dressing notes to reflect 2-corner floor + 4-edge walls.
OUT OF SCOPE:
3-color Wang (3+ families competing) — binary per-family stays.
Sub-variant random pick within a Wang index — future polish.
Migration of cliff face + block walls to 2-corner. Stays 4-edge for those (hybrid per §6.2).
Animated transitions (grass shimmer crossing into path mud). Static.
Visual editor for variant authoring. Procedural code authors.
